title: The name Ardenna
text:
Hey Claude, how do you pronounce Ardenna?  

"Ardenna" is pronounced ar-DEN-uh (with the stress on the middle syllable).
It's the genus name for shearwaters - those incredible long-distance seabirds that spend most of their lives at sea, gliding low over the waves. A fitting name for a bluewater cruising yacht!
author: Doug

title: Looking for a 1,500nm logbook entry?
text:
We will be heading south this autumn to the Dominican Republic and are looking for crew to join the fun. This is not a potential or a maybe, but a confirmed passage departing Newport for Puerto Bahía Marina in Samaná, DR, this November 2026.

Over Halloween weekend, we will meet with other members of the Bluewater Sailing Club in Newport, RI, to prep, plan, and commune before heading out to sea together. Specifically, we will be at a dock at the Newport Yachting Center October 30 – November 1, leaving (weather permitting) for what will be a 9–12 day passage directly to the DR.

Are you interested in joining us? This will be a fun offshore passage with a wide range of weather, currents, and marine life. We will embrace the cold New England weather with layers of wool under our bibs and hoodies while enjoying the warmth of the full-boat Webasto hydronic heater, knowing it won’t be long before it is almost too hot.

Leaving Newport, we will head East to cut the Gulf Stream and then start a straight shot South, taking Bermuda to port. Within a few days, the weather will warm, and we will ditch the wool and start washing the salt off our sunnies. A few more days after that, you will need sunscreen for your legs as shorts become the order of the day. Once we get South of Florida, it will just be hot!

Weather windows open and close quickly in New England in autumn, so some flexibility regarding the Samaná arrival will be needed; however, the total trip should take between 8–12 days. We greatly prefer to sail but will motor to keep things moving, charge batteries, and make hot water. Everyone will have their own bunk and locker, and a freshwater shower every day or two. We will pay for food, customs, visas, and transportation to the Santo Domingo airport. You will handle the trip to Newport (we can pick you up at Boston Logan) and the trip home from the DR.
author: Doug

title: You've got to love maintenance
text: It's been a busy spring on Ardenna not for sailing but certainly for maintenance.  She's in excellent shape as confirmed by the Autumn survey but before we start long passages it was time to get replace some of the big stuff like standing rigging, rebed chainplates, and fresh bottom paint.  These items along with new topside paint, a new code zero and jib from Elvstrom, and a few new pieces of running rigging were completed by Maine Yacht Center.  Since then, I've managed to install the water maker, break the water maker, break the refreigerator compressor control unit, repair the water maker, and repair the refrigeration line seals and control unit.  If you need help with a Schenker Ready 60 or Danfoss keel cooled K50F then call me.  I've now done it and likely still have the tools.
author: Doug

title: Samaná logistics
text:
Good day everyone and welcome to the Ardenna DR Caravan!  

Marella and I are very excited to have you all join us on this fun, ten(ish)-day passage from Newport, RI to Samaná, Dominican Republic.  While autumn in New England can be a bit unpredictable, here is the current plan:

October 29 leave Salem, MA early for Sandwich, MA

October 30 leave Sandwich, MA early to ride the current through the Cape Cod Canal to Newport, RI staying at the Newport Yachting Center

October 31 dinner with other crews in the Bluewater Sailing Club Caribbean Challenge rally.  They’re leaving at the same time as Ardenna, making for Bermuda and Antigua.

November 1 leave Newport for Samaná, DR

November 9 - 11 (tentative) arrival at Marina Puerto Bahía (www.puertobahia.do)

Arrival to November 14 Relax, shower, a little laundry, a beer, and pool time, whatever suits. 

Morning November 15 We will be leaving for the airport back to Boston. You are all welcome to join us in the car service to Las Americas International Airport, Santo Domingo (SDQ airport identifier) or can stay at the Bannister Hotel (https://www.thebannisterhotel.com) or a local AirBnB.  

Marella and I will be heading to Salem on October 28th to do final preparation so feel free to ride up with us or meet us at the marina, Safe Harbor Hawthorne Cove (White St, Salem, MA). If you would rather meet us in Newport, RI on October 30 or 31 that works too.  We’ll do general orientation to the boat and systems once we are all together and as we are underway.  

The boat: Ardenna is a 2007 Contest 50CS with comfortable berthing for six leaving everyone with their own bunk and locker space.  The refrigerator/freezer is a decent size and there is a ton of storage in lockers and under the sole and seating.  We have a water maker putting out 12 gallons an hour, water heater, and 185 gallons of tankage meaning we are still on track for a rinse off or shower every day or two in one of the two heads.  We have 800 watts of solar and plenty of places to charge phones, headphones, etc.  as well as different adapter and charger options.

Connectivity: Ardenna is equipped with Starlink allowing us to pull down weather forecasts, emails, texts, and podcasts once a day. We won’t be downloading Netflix or surfing YouTube but it’s reasonable to assume you’ll be in regular contact with loved ones. We’ll be tracking progress online as well - more to come as we get closer to departure.  The sextant is coming along so we can take turns at noon sights. 

Packing and prep: The first few days out of Newport will likely be on the cool side meaning you will want a sweater or hoodie, long pants, and generally layer options. Once we’re clear of the Gulf Stream getting closer to Bermuda it will warm up and a few days after that, you’ll want shorts and a short sleeve shirt. While we have heaps of storage, please pack in a collapsible bag.  You’ll have a locker to organize your gear and we will stow your bag out of the way.  If you have foulies please bring them.  We have a spare jacket and bibs and can share if you are a size medium.  Once it’s warm, bare feet work well but you will want a pair of non-marking shoes to wear in the cockpit and saloon. 

Medications: We’ve arranged for on demand emergency medical coverage from George Washington University Medical Center should we have any issues and carry a well-stocked med kit including Dramamine, painkillers, and antibiotics.  If you get seasick or think you might, talk to your physician about Scopolamine patches.  We’ve had crew in the past use them with great results but do not carry them on the boat.

The passage: We’ve organized for weather routing from Marine Weather Center (www.mwxc.com) and will be getting regular support once underway.  This said, the plan generally is to leave Newport, sailing ESE for a day or so to cut across the Gulf Stream and then head to Samaná on a rhumb line, SSE. If we ever wanted or needed, we’d have Bermuda as a bailout point.  We can talk it out together but we’re thinking of a two person watch schedule with three hours on, six hours off.

Everyone will need to use an assigned Mustang Survival PFD, strap, and tether so do not bring your own PFD.  The reason is all PFDs on Ardenna have a locator beacon installed that deploys upon inflation, sounds an onboard alarm, and shows the survivor location on the chartplotter.

Food, provisioning, prep: Marella is the master of provisioning so more to come later coordinating menu and snack prep as well as going through dietary restrictions.  Ardenna has a three-burner gas stove with oven, microwave, electric kettle, coffee maker, and toaster along with a good sized combination refrigerator/freezer.  Each berth has pillows, linens, and blankets for you. 

Customs: Marella and I will sort formalities upon arrival in Samaná but you’ll need a passport with at least six (6) months additional time upon arrival.  Let me know if you are not travelling on a US Passport.  Other than the liquor cabinet, we will all (of us) be drug and weapon free, so we fly through customs without drama and quickly get to the showers and infinity pools.  

More to come over the coming weeks and months but please let us know if you have any questions or concerns.  We’re very excited to have you join us.
author: Düg
